caption: Gradient: the angle round the centre, plus a clock, as a turning colour wheel
why: A ramp from 0 to 1 is the start of most colour layouts: a fade across, a glow from the middle, a wheel. Gradient makes the common shapes of ramp in one node, so you do not have to build them from coordinates and maths.

Pick the shape with a setting: linear and quadratic run along x, diagonal across both, radial goes round the centre and spherical out from it. Its neighbours: Coords gives the raw coordinates the ramps are made from (u is the linear ramp itself); Colour ramp turns a 0..1 into your own colours; Gradient is the 0..1.
steps: **Coords** `centred x` and `centred y` - the place measured from the centre, -1..1 - go into **x** and **y**. The round shapes need the centred coordinates; the straight ones read x as a plain ramp.
**shape** is radial: the value is the angle round the centre, 0..1 for a full turn.
A clock (**Time** times 0.2) is added to it, and the sum is the **Palette**'s index: the palette goes once round the wheel, and the clock turns it.
Change the shape and the same clock does something different - see below.

try.label: Spherical
try.text: shape spherical: bright at the centre falling to the edge - with the clock added, rings of colour pour outward from the middle.

try.label: Diagonal
try.text: shape diagonal: a ramp from one corner to the other, so the colours scroll across at an angle.

try.label: Quadratic
try.text: shape quadratic: a curved ramp along x - the colours bunch together at one side and spread out at the other.
